He died about four hundred years ago, in the fifth century of the Hijra, while seated in a place of his shrine, which was the Bistamiyya. Someone who witnessed it told me, from among the students of knowledge of the Persians, whom I do not accuse of this, and it is a famous and widely transmitted matter in their lands, not dependent on the witnessing of one specific person. He said: I visited him more than once, and he has an awe that prevents the believer from approaching him closely enough to see his face, just as Allah, exalted is He, indicated something similar by His saying: ﴿But you would have turned from them in flight and been filled with terror of them﴾ (Qur'an 18:18). He said: On one occasion there was with us a student of knowledge from the people of Kayland, who was not a believer, and he said: This is only a kind of sleight of hand, by which the minds of the rabble are deceived. He said: So he approached him boldly, touched his chest, and looked into his face, and he was struck immediately, and he did not return except carried. He remained for some time in the madrasa where he had been studying in the city of Shamakhi. And he informed us that Shaykh Damdamki said to him when he touched him: "Had you not been among the people of knowledge, you would have perished." And [he said] that [the shaykh] was a man with a light beard. He said: I have repented to Allah, exalted is He, and I have become one of the believers in what he is upon, that it is true, and I do not deny any of the marvels (karamat) of the saints. The narrator said: He was buried three times, one of which was by the order of Timurlane, and he is found sitting in the morning in the same state he is in now. And Allah is the Granter of success toward what is right.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 15:

When He (glorified is He) indicated, by His saying ﴿Have they not seen what is before them and behind them?﴾ [Saba': 9], and so on, His power over what He wills in the heavens and the earth, to deal with whomever He wills among those in them as He wills, with favour toward whoever gives thanks and with justice toward whoever disbelieves, (p-474) He indicated this by what He related of the reports of some of those who were thankful. He concluded with the death of His prophet Sulayman ibn Dawud, the grateful son of a grateful father (peace be upon them both), and the sign in it that shows that none but Him knows the unseen, so that this would yield that none but Him is able to do all that He wills. The death of the earlier prophets necessarily led to disorder after them, because their signs were lost with their passing, unlike the sign of the Qur'an, which remains through the passing of ages and times, for every human, angel and jinn, whose herald proclaims it before the witnesses: "Is there anyone who opposes or contends?" Therefore this community was preserved, while others were lost in dark valleys. He followed it with another proof, a witnessed one, concerning the sign of ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them﴾ [Saba': 9], regarding a people whose full righteousness was through Sulayman, peace be upon him. After him their affairs fell into disorder, and their remembrance became one of the wonders of the world when their gratitude was lost. The sequel to their story following what preceded it is that the family of Dawud, peace be upon him, gave thanks, so He subjected to them the mountains, the birds, the metals and other things that no one else would hope for. They neglected gratitude, so He withheld from them and took from them what they had not feared losing: their waters, their trees and other things. Thus He, exalted is He, said, indicating by its emphasis the magnitude of what they were in, and that it is in the utmost degree of indication of power and of all the attributes of perfection, and that the deeds of Quraysh are the deeds of one who denies what their story indicates (p-475) of this: ﴿Certainly there was for Saba' [a sign] in their dwelling place﴾. That is, the famous township that used to prostrate to the sun, whom Allah guided through the hand of Sulayman, peace be upon him. The wisdom of Qunbul's pausing on their hamza (al-tasmin, pausing by suppressing the hamza) is to indicate the ease, comfort, and pleasant living they were in, which bears fruit in rest, tranquillity, calm and peace. Perhaps the majority's reading of it with tanwin indicates something similar, while the reading of Abu 'Amr and al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir with the prohibition (of tanwin, i.e., as a diptote) indicates their return, with what they came to of bad condition, to the usual state of those lands in barrenness, scarcity of vegetation and thirst. ﴿In their dwelling place﴾, that is, which is in the utmost abundance. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim made it singular, indicating [that] because of the intense connection of benefits and amenities, it is like a single dwelling. Al-Kisa'i read the kaf with kasra, indicating [that it is in the utmost suitability and softness for them], and the other two read it with fatha, indicating [the spirit and comfort within it]. Their land was in the region of Ma'rib in the lands of Yemen. Hamza al-Kirmani said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: three farsakhs from San'a'. It was the most fertile, the most pleasant, and the most fruitful of lands, to the extent that a woman would place the basket on her head and walk among the trees, and the basket would fill without her touching anything with her hand. (p-476) Their water used to flow out of a mountain, so they built a dam in it and made for it three gates. They would direct the water to their vineyards from the upper, middle and lower gates. Al-Razi said: the woman would go out with her spindle and her basket on her head, working at her spinning, and would not return to her house until her basket was full [of] fruit. Abu Hayyan said in al-Nahr: When Bilqis reigned, her people fought over the water of their valley, so she left her kingdom and stayed in her palace. They pressed her to return, but she refused, so they said: "You will return, or we will surely kill you." She said to them: "You have no intellect, and you do not obey me." They said: "We will obey you." So she returned to their valley. Whenever they were rained upon, the flood would come to them from a distance of three days' journey, so she commanded that it be dammed: what was between the two mountains was blocked with a dyke of stone and bitumen, she held back the water behind the dam, and made for it gates, some above others, and built behind it a basin with twelve outlets according to the number of their rivers, and the water would come out for them in equal shares. Al-Mas'udi said in the introductions to Murawj al-Dhahab, shortly before the Prophetic biography, in discussing soothsayers: it was among the most fertile and productive lands of Yemen, the sweetest and most wholesome of waters, and the most abundant in gardens, (p-477) and the rider who travelled diligently in that condition across its breadth for more than a month would cover the same distance, going from its beginning until he reached its end, with the sun never facing him and the shade never leaving him, because the land was concealed by trees, overtaken by them and encircled by them. Its people were in the most pleasant, most elevated, most agreeable and most abundant of lives, in the height of fertility, pleasant air, clear open space, flowing water, strength of power and unity of word. Then he related a lengthy account of their history, the ruin of what had been their monuments, and their dispersal in the lands and scattering among the people. ﴿A sign﴾, that is, a manifest indication of Our power over what We will. Then he explained the sign with His saying: ﴿Two gardens﴾, adjoining the road, ﴿on the right and on the left﴾, that is, connected orchards, interlaced gardens and intertwined meadows, so that everything from every side was one garden, because of the intense connection of one part to another, on the right of every traveller and on his left, wherever he travelled through their lands, with no unused place in them. Al-Baghawi said: on the right of their valley and on its left; the two gardens had encircled that valley. He indicated the generosity of those gardens and the abundance of good in them by His saying: ﴿Eat﴾, that is, their lands need nothing beyond being told: "Eat." ﴿Of the provision of your Lord﴾, that is, the Benefactor toward you, who brought forth for you from them everything you desire. ﴿And give thanks to Him﴾, that is, devote your thanks to Him by acting in what pleases Him with the favour He has bestowed, so that He may continue the blessing for you. Then he resumed the magnification of (p-478) that by His saying: ﴿A good land﴾, that is, of noble soil, good air, free from vermin and pests, whose inhabitant needs nothing that follows him and hinders him from gratitude. Ibn Zayd said: there are no fleas, no mosquitoes, no scorpions and no snakes in it; their clothes do not become infested with lice, and their animals do not tire. He indicated that no one can estimate it at its true worth by His saying: ﴿And a Lord Forgiving﴾, that is, for the sin of whoever is grateful to Him and falls short, by erasing both the trace and the substance of what he fell short in, so that He does not punish for it or rebuke for it. Were it not for that, He would not have bestowed upon you what you are in, and He would have destroyed you for your sins. Some people of Yemen told me that it is today a desert near San'a' in Yemen, he said: in some of it there are large raisins made from grapes, of the size of pearls, bordering the lands of al-Sham, and it is in the utmost clarity, as if it were pieces of mastic, and it has no seeds at all.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 16:

When their wantonness, which required them to turn away from gratitude, resulted from this bounty, He indicated this by His words: ﴿But they turned away﴾. When their turning away resulted in His abhorrence of them, He explained it by His words: ﴿So We sent against them the flood of the dam (sayl al-'Arim)﴾. He indicated by the particle of elevation (*'alā*, "upon") that this was the sending of a punishment after a manifestation of majesty. He said: ﴿against them the flood of the dam﴾, that is, a torrent of rain, overwhelming, harmful, severe, abundant, sharp in effect, extreme in harm, which nothing can repel and no stratagem can prevent, whether by a barrier or otherwise, due to its *'aramah*, which is intensity and strength. It thus destroyed for them everything from which they benefited. Abu Hayyan said: God sent against them a blind mole-rat (*jurdh*), a burrowing creature that multiplied within it, also called the *khuld*, which gnawed at it bit by bit. Then God sent a flood into that valley, which carried away the dam. It is narrated that it was of such magnitude and abundance of water that it filled the space between the two mountains, and carried away the gardens and many people who had been unable to flee. When some of them drowned and some were saved, they were scattered and dispersed, until the Arabs made them a proverb, saying: "They scattered like the hands of Saba'" (*tafarraqū aydiya Saba'*), and the Aws and Khazraj were of them. This occurred in the interval (*fatrah*) between 'Isa and our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And We exchanged for them their two gardens﴾, that is, We made for them in their place ﴿two gardens﴾ which were at the utmost opposite of their two gardens. For this reason He described them by His words, to inform that applying the term "two gardens" to them is a verbal correspondence (*mushākalah lafziyyah*) used for mockery of them: ﴿bearing bitter fruit (dhawātay ukul khamt)﴾, that is, fruit ﴿of khamt﴾. The reading of the majority is with tanwin on *ukul*, which is more emphatic in mockery than the reading of Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub with the idafah.

Since *khamt* is shared between animals and humans in eating and avoiding it, and God knows best what He intended by it: it is a kind of tamarisk (*arak*) with an edible fruit; every bitter, thorny tree; the sour or bitter of everything; every plant that has taken on a taste of bitterness so that it cannot be eaten or it is impossible to eat; a fruit called "hyena's pudenda" (*faswat al-dab'*) in the form of a poppy seed, which is rubbed and not benefited from; and the small yield of any tree. He mentioned what pertains to the animals by which human sustenance is maintained, saying: ﴿and tamarisk (athl)﴾, that is, and two kinds of athl, which is a tree with no fruit, a type of tamarisk (*tarfā'*). Then He mentioned what pertains to humans, saying: ﴿and a little lote-tree (sidr)﴾, that is, the jujube (*nabq*), ﴿little﴾. This indicates that other than the lote-tree, namely what has no benefit, or whose benefit is mixed with turbidity more than the lote-tree's, is included. Abu Hayyan said: al-Farra' interpreted this *sidr* as the *samur* (acacia). He said: al-Azhari said: there are two kinds of *sidr*: a *sidr* from which no benefit is derived, whose leaves are not suitable for washing, and which has an astringent fruit that is not eaten; this is what is called *ad-dall*; and a *sidr* that grows on water, whose fruit is the jujube (*nabq*) and whose leaf is used for washing (*ghusul*), resembling the 'unnāb (jujube).

The promise was previously made in al-Baqarah to explain what the entry of the preposition with the root *badal* implies, since the states differ in it between *ibdāl*, *tabdīl*, *istibdāl*, *tabaddul*, and other forms; these involve many turns of meaning and are of confused matter. Our shaykh, the verifier of his age, the judge of the Shafi'is in the Egyptian lands, Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Qayati, may God have mercy on him, has verified them, and he said in what I recorded from him, and most of which he mentioned in his commentary on the introduction of al-Nawawi's *Minhaj*, may God have mercy on him: Know that this root, namely *b*, *d*, *l* in this order, may be mentioned with its two correlates only, and may be mentioned with other things, and may not be so. If it is limited to the two, the two may be mentioned with *tabaddul* and *istibdāl*, one of them accompanied by *bi'* (with), as in God's words: ﴿Do you exchange that which is lower for that which is better?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61], and in His words: ﴿And whoever substitutes disbelief for faith﴾ [al-Baqarah: 108], the verse. Thus the *bā'* enters upon what is left, and the verb transitively takes the adopted correlate directly. The two may also be mentioned with *tabdīl* and *ibdāl*, one of them joined with *bā'*, so the *bā'* enters upon what is obtained, and the verb transitively reaches what is left directly. Al-Azhari transmitted from Tha'lab: "I replaced (*baddaltu*) the ring with the hoop" when you melt it and make it a hoop; "I replaced the hoop with the ring" when you melt it and make it a ring; "I substituted (*abdaltu*) the ring with the hoop" when you remove this and put that in its place. Al-Harawi, in *al-Gharibayn*, related from Ibn 'Arafah, meaning Nifawayh, that he said: *tabdīl* is changing a thing from its state, and *ibdāl* is placing a thing in the place of another. Its verification is that the meaning of *tabdīl* is change even if no replacement is brought, as mentioned in *al-Sihah*, and as the implication of Ibn 'Arafah's words indicates. So where the two correlates are mentioned and it is said: "I replaced this with that," the result is that you took that and gave this. Thus when it is said "he replaced the thing with other," its meaning is that he changed the thing for another, i.e., left the first and took the second; so the *bā'* enters upon what is taken, not what is removed. The meaning of substituting a thing with another returns to removing the thing and placing another in its place, so the *bā'* enters upon what is taken in place of what is removed. *Tabdīl*, even with only the two correlates, has another usage, transitively taking two objects directly, as in God's words: ﴿Those, God will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], and ﴿So your Lord desired that He replace for them something better than him in purity﴾ [al-Kahf: 81], the verse, meaning He makes good deeds a replacement for evil deeds and gives them, in place of what was theirs, something better. It may also not mention what was removed, as in God's words: ﴿We replaced them with other skins﴾ [al-Nisa': 56]. The meaning of *tabaddul* and *istibdāl* is taking a thing in place of another. So when you say "I substituted (*istabdaltu*) this for that," or "I exchanged (*tabaddaltu*) this for that," the result is that you took this and left that. If the two are not limited to them, but other things are mentioned with them, one of them accompanied by the preposition, and *tabdīl* is mentioned, as in God's words ﴿And We exchanged for them their two gardens for two gardens﴾, the verb transitively takes two objects directly: the object for which it is done, the object taken directly, and the object removed, with which the substitution is made by *bā'*, as in "He replaced his fear with security" (*baddalahu bi-khawfihi amnan*), meaning: he removed his fear to security. It may also take the removed object, in this situation, with *min*, as in "he replaced him from his fear with security" (*baddalahu min khawfihi amnan*). *Tabdīl* also has another usage, transitively taking one object, like "I replaced (*baddaltu*) the thing," that is, I changed it. God said: ﴿So whoever alters it after he has heard it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 181]. Here there is something that must be noticed: a thing may be taken relative to and by comparison with one thing, and left relative to and by comparison with another, as when a person gives another person a thing and takes its substitute from him. The first thing is taken by the second person and left by the first, and the correlate is the reverse. It is therefore valid to express it with *tabaddul* and *tabdīl*, and each one is considered according to what suits it. The difficulty we intended is what occasioned some lengthiness. Ended. And God knows best.

When he reported this devastation and reduction after they had been in that great dominion, he magnified its matter by placing the object first, to show that it is among the things one should be most concerned to understand, and said: ﴿That﴾, that is, this great recompense of lofty rank in the matter of destruction, ﴿We recompensed them﴾ by what We possess of greatness, ﴿for what they disbelieved﴾, that is, they covered over (p. 484) the clear proof.

Since it is the settled custom among people of lofty resolve, who are most practiced in confronting champions, to exaggerate the punishment of one who does evil after good and who answers favour with ingratitude, because of what such conduct leaves burning in hearts time and again, and blow upon blow, God, glorified be He, conducted the matter according to this custom. He said, alluding to this with the form of *mufa'ala* (the reciprocal verbal pattern), counting any other recompense as nothing in comparison to His, as a threat that splits hearts, restrains souls, and leaves necks submissive and heads bowed: ﴿And do We recompense﴾, that is, this recompense which takes the form of punishment, ﴿except the ungrateful﴾, that is, the one who exaggerates in disbelief. The reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim is ﴿nujazi﴾ with a *nun*, in keeping with the style of greatness that precedes it, and ﴿al-kafur﴾ in the accusative. Al-Farra' said: "The believer is rewarded (*yujza*) and not recompensed (*yujaza*)." It is as if he indicated that the punishment of the wrongdoer is for his deed, so it takes the form of *mufa'ala*, whereas the reward of the obedient is a bounty from God, not because of his deed, since his deed is itself a blessing from God. This does not contradict multiplication.

Al-Qushayri said: Likewise, among people there is one who is in ease of circumstance, in continued success, in goodness of heart, and in favourable times. Then he commits a slip, or behaves discourteously, or follows a desire, without knowing the worth of what he is in. So his state changes for him, and there remains neither time nor state, neither joy nor union. The day grows dark for him, though his nights were once lit with wondrous lights. (p. 485)

When he had completed the account of the gardens, by which livelihood is sustained as both blessing and punishment, he followed it with an account of their inhabitants, saying: ﴿And We made﴾, i.e., by virtue of Our greatness. By omitting the preposition, he drew attention to the cultivation of all those lands through building and benefit, saying: ﴿between them﴾, i.e., between the villages of the people of Saba', ﴿and between the towns﴾, i.e., cities or what is less than them, ﴿which We had blessed﴾, i.e., with a blessing toward which We took special care, like one who competes with another in utmost greatness, ﴿therein﴾, i.e., by making them places of knowledge and provision through the prophets and the chosen friends of God, and they are the lands of al-Sham, ﴿visible villages﴾, i.e., from the land of al-Sham, on the noblest and highest parts of the earth and what is firm and elevated of it, because building there is more durable, walking there is easier, and enjoying the sight of all the gardens and their freshness is more possible from them. So they are visible to the eyes among those gardens, like bright stars, while being so close together that some of them can be seen from others, with abundance of wealth there, pride, benefit, and help for travelers. Al-Baghawi said: there were four thousand and seven hundred contiguous villages from Saba' (p-486) to al-Sham.

Since, despite this description, there may have been hardship for the traveler there, owing to the lack of suitable places for resting at midday and for spending the night, He removed this by His saying: ﴿And We measured therein the travel﴾, i.e., We set it by measures that are most gentle to the traveler in his stopping, whenever he wishes, by night or by day, according to what the customs of travelers have established. For this reason, it is fitting that it be said to its people and to those who dwell in it, as a favor: ﴿Travel﴾. The indication of their great proximity is His saying: ﴿therein﴾. It also indicates their abundance, the length of their distances, and their suitability for travel at any time one wishes. He placed first what is more indicative of safety and more moderate for travel in hot lands, saying: ﴿nights﴾. He pointed to the abundance of shade, moisture, and the temperateness with which travel is possible throughout the day, saying: ﴿and days﴾, i.e., at whatever time you wish. It also indicates its great safety at all times for everyone who encounters a difficulty, saying: ﴿secure﴾, i.e., from fear and weariness, or loss, thirst, or hunger.

(p-487) When the account of these attributes, which call for the utmost gratitude because of the favours they contain, was complete, He indicated their wantonness toward the blessing they had been given. They made these favours a cause of impatience and weariness, by saying, ﴿So they said﴾, in the form of a supplication: ﴿"Our Lord, make distant﴾, meaning, O You who nurture us, ﴿"the distance between our journeys"﴾, meaning, make the distance great and lengthen it. This is according to the recitation of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Hisham from Ibn 'Amir, with the ʿayn doubled (bāʿid, shaddad the ʿayn) and the dal sukun (bāʿid, "baʿid" with a sukun on the dal). This has the same meaning as the recitation of the rest of the readers other than Ya'qub, ﴿bā'id﴾, which requires its extension and lengthening, ﴿"between our journeys"﴾, meaning, between our villages in which we travel. The meaning is: so that people would be few, and what belongs to each person of these gardens would be many times what belongs to him now, and we would carry provisions, ride the swift camels, hang our weapons, and choose fine mounts. Some of them, as if they were of the opposite inclination to these people, multiplied the distance between every two villages. So he said, as Ya'qub recited, "Rabbuna" (our Lord) with a damma on the ra' (as the subject, mubtada'), and "baʿʿada" as a past-tense verb (as the predicate, khabar). Thus he belittled that blessing which had come according to the rule of wisdom, and desired that those villages be continuous. ﴿And they wronged﴾ themselves, in that they counted the blessing as a curse and the kindness as an offence. ﴿Themselves﴾: at times by making their dwellings few, and at times by making their fruits few. Thus that caused the change of their condition to a state of desolation in proportion to the intimacy they had been in. This is the meaning of ﴿So We made them﴾, meaning, by what We have of majesty, ﴿into tales﴾, meaning, people would recount their description generation after generation, because of its terror. ﴿And We scattered them﴾, meaning, a scattering befitting majesty. They had no custom except compliance, so they were scattered ﴿in every scattering﴾, meaning, in every manner of scattering, as a garment is torn, to such an extent that they became a proverbial example up to this time, (p-488) and it is said of one whose affair has been broken up: "They have scattered like the hands of Saba'" (taqarraqu aydi Saba').

Since each of these two states of theirs, prosperity and ruin, was a striking matter pointing to many things, among them the power over the Hour, which is the aim of the surah, moving from blessing to hellfire, and gathering (the dead) except what a person does not want, as the people of Saba' were gathered to many regions of the lands, as is well known in their story. He said, drawing attention to this and as a conclusion, emphasizing it to call attention to careful consideration of it, because of what it contains of indications of attributes of perfection: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning, in that great matter, ﴿are signs﴾, meaning, very clear indications of the power of God, Exalted, over disposing of what is before them and behind them of the heavens and the earth, by bringing into existence and annihilating essences and attributes, by sinking and transforming. For there is no difference between one extraordinary event and another. Also, their wantonness toward that blessing, to the point that they became weary of it and prayed for its removal, is evidence that a human being, as long as he is alive, is in a blessing that obliges him to be grateful for it, whatever it may be, even if he sees it as an affliction. For because of what he has been created with of restlessness, he often sees blessings as curses and pleasure as pain. For this reason He ended the verse with "patient" (ṣabbār) in the form of intensification.

Since patience is restraining the self from its corrupt aims and blinding desires, and opposing desire is the hardest and most difficult thing for the self, and blessings cause arrogance and transgression, corruption and distraction, it was difficult to turn souls to gratitude (p-489) after they had bolted in the excess of blessings. Quraysh had shared with Saba' in what has been mentioned, and had added to them the abundance of living and the ease of the arrival of provision, with what made them beloved and made their land beloved to the worshippers through the supplication of their father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), together with the security of the land, the nobility of lineage, and the greatness of rank, as indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And God presents a parable: a town that was secure and at rest﴾ [al-Nahl: 112], and the verse. He, Exalted, said, warning them of a punishment like theirs: ﴿For every patient, grateful one﴾, meaning, from all the children of Adam, indicating by the intensive form all of that, and that whoever does not have patience and gratitude in his nature cannot manage that, and that whoever does not have patience in his nature has missed gratitude.

Since the meaning is: [there are] signs in [the matter of] your opposing Iblis, so that you do not give credence to his assumption about their being led astray, when he said: ﴿Surely if You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾ [al-Isra: 62]. He emphasized this to reject anyone's supposition that Iblis's assumption about them had been correct. ﴿And indeed﴾, that is, there were in that signs preventing one from following Satan, while the situation was that he ﴿had indeed confirmed﴾ [his assumption]. Since his misleading them, in causing them to commit what their intellects testify is error, was a dominant one over them, He indicated this with the particle of elevation (isti'la', the sense of being over or above), so He said: ﴿over them﴾, that is, over the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him.

(p-490) Since the context affirms the greatness of God, what He has of good, and His complete disposal of affairs, which calls one to turn toward Him and to confine aspirations to Him, He expressed the name with the words "Iblis" (the Almighty's words), which derives from balas (ruin, despair), meaning that which has no good in it, and iblas (dejection), which is despair of every good, so that this would be greater in rebuke and reproach. ﴿His assumption﴾, that is, in his saying: ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾ [al-Isra: 62]; ﴿and I will surely mislead them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 39]; ﴿except Your sincere servants﴾ [al-Hijr: 40]; ﴿and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf: 17]. It is as if, when he said that on the basis of supposition, his supposition demanded [that it be true], so [God] confirmed it in carrying out his scheme, until that supposition became true. This is according to the reading of the majority (qira'at al-jama'ah), with the lightened form. As for the reading of the Kufans, with the doubled form, the meaning is that He made his supposition, which could have been disproved before it was verified, true, such that no one could disprove it. For this reason, God, glory be to Him, made the following statement its consequence: ﴿so they followed him﴾, that is, with utmost effort, through natural inclination and the pleasure that necessitates pulling toward and hastening [to it], some of them in disbelief and some in disobedience in general.

Since those spoken of were the masses of people, He made the exception definite (by the article) because the saved are few, so He said: ﴿except a group﴾, that is, people who have the ability to divide the word of the people of disbelief and disperse their gathering, even if they are, relative to them, like a white hair (p-491) on a black bull's hide, ﴿of the believers﴾, that is, those firmly rooted in faith, so they were sincere to God and devoted in worshipping Him. As for others, they inclined with him. Among them were those who were few in lapses and those who were many, in minor and major failings.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 21:

Since that might give the impression that Iblis has some authority of his own, he negated it with His words: ﴿and not﴾, meaning, while the situation is that he ﴿had﴾ at all ﴿over them﴾, meaning those who followed him or others, ﴿any authority﴾, meaning any compelling dominion over anything in any way. He stressed the negation of what is true by saying ﴿from authority﴾, because he is like them in being a servant, weak, subdued, humbled, fearful and repelled. Al-Qushayri said: "He is empowered, but if he were able to lead others astray, he would be able to keep himself on guidance." ﴿Except﴾, meaning, but rather, ﴿We gave him power over them by Our authority and made him master of their leadership by Our subjugation.” He expressed the distinction, which is the cause of knowledge, by means of knowledge, saying ﴿that We may know﴾, meaning, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿who believes﴾, meaning brings about belief in God, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾, meaning so that Our knowledge of that is connected in the world of witnessing, in the state of its distinction, with a connection by which proof is established within the customary ways of human beings, just as it was connected in the world of the unseen, ﴿from one who is in doubt about it﴾, meaning about the Hereafter. So for him no belief in it is ever renewed at all, because doubt is a container that encompasses him. He used "illa" (except) in place of "lakin" (but rather) to indicate (p-٤٩٢) that He gave him complete empowerment, by which he became like one who has true authority.

Since this might create the impression of a deficiency in knowledge or in power, he said, pointing out that He, glory be to Him, facilitated for the Prophet (ﷺ) by multiplying this sincere group and making most of them from his community: ﴿And your Lord﴾, meaning the one who is good to you by disgracing Satan through your prophethood and expelling him from your community, ﴿is over all things﴾ among the responsible and others ﴿Guardian﴾, meaning a guardian of the most complete preservation, encompassing them, governing them in a manner of exaltedness, with His perfect knowledge and comprehensive power. So neither Satan nor anyone else does anything except by His knowledge and His permission.

When Glorified He had established for Himself, and for His Most Holy Essence, the dominion over the heavens and the earth and other than them, as you have seen, and had adduced proofs for it that cannot be challenged with any criticism, as you have heard, and since the greatest aim was *tawhid* (affirmation of God's oneness), for it is the foundation upon which every good is built, He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, [O] most knowledgeable of creation! By establishing proofs against these people who associated partners with God, of a thing whose worthlessness no one with even a little sense doubts: ﴿Call upon those whom you claimed﴾, that is, that they are gods, as you call upon God, especially in times of hardship. He omitted the two objects of *za'ama* ("to claim"), namely their pronoun and their being called gods, to signal the repugnance and abhorrence of this. What is mentioned in the verse is neither an object nor standing in the place of an object, because the meaning would be corrupted. He then made their worthlessness clear by saying: ﴿besides God﴾, that is, the One who has gathered all greatness, such that none of the things He has established for Himself belongs to them. So let them do something like it, or let them nullify something of what He has done.

Since their answer to this was silence, from incapacity and bewilderment, Glorified He Himself answered on their behalf, indicating that the answer of everyone who reflects is unhesitating. He expressed them in the wording used for one who has knowledge of their standing in that position, or because some of those who were claimed to be divine were among those who have knowledge, saying: ﴿They do not possess﴾, that is, now, and nothing of that will come to them anew at all.

Since the intended meaning was to exaggerate their worthlessness in the manner the Arabs understand, He said: ﴿the weight of an atom﴾. And since generality was intended, He expressed it with: ﴿in the heavens﴾, and emphasized it by saying: ﴿nor in the earth﴾, because the "heaven" is what is above and the "earth" is what is below, and the heavens are within the Throne, and the earth is within the heaven. Thus that negation encompassed both and everything in them, of essence and of attribute, up to the Throne, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.

Since this was apparent in negating pure dominion free from any admixture of partnership, He also negated partnership, emphasizing it as a rebuke to them concerning what they claim, saying: ﴿And they have no share in them﴾, that is, in the heavens and the earth, nor in what is in them. He went further in the negation and said: (p-494) ﴿of partnership﴾, [that is] in creation, nor in sovereignty, nor in ownership. He emphasized the negation by affirming the preposition. Since among what is in the heavens and the earth are the souls of these idols, and their dominion over anything of their own souls has been negated, or over what Glorified He has placed in them of power or benefit, it followed that they cannot have the ability to help others. Since explicitness gives greater awe to souls, a shaking to hearts, and a cutting off of hopes, so that there remains no firm grasp nor weak one, He said: ﴿And He has not among them﴾, that is, God has not among them, and He emphasized the negation by affirming the preposition, saying: ﴿any supporter﴾, that is, any helper in anything that He wills. How then can it be valid, with this total incapacity, that they be called upon as He is called upon, hoped in as He is hoped in, and worshipped as He is worshipped?

When the remaining categories of benefit had been mentioned, and the intent of intercession is its effect rather than its essence, He negated it by saying: ﴿And intercession does not benefit with Him﴾, that is, at any time whatsoever, ﴿intercession﴾, that is, in any manner or by any means, ﴿except for one whom﴾. Since the veil's density is greater in awe, and the passive form is more indicative of the density of the veil, he said, in the reading of Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, by making the verbal noun (masdar) the principal element of the sentence and attributing the verb to it: ﴿He has permitted﴾, that is, permission has come from Him ﴿for him﴾ through whomever of His hosts He wills, by one intermediary or more, that he may intercede for another, or that another may intercede for him. The reading of the rest, with the active form of the verb, indicates majesty from another aspect, namely that no one can encroach upon Him in any way whatsoever, rather that He Himself, glorified is He, must specify the permission; otherwise there is no capacity to act against Him at all.

Since it is known that those held in a place of dread for presentation before a feared king, whenever one of them is called by name and it is said, "Where is so-and-so?", his heart is struck with terror and he may even faint, therefore it is known from what has preceded that whenever the call comes from Him, exalted is He, in that station in which every nation is seen kneeling, the intercessors and those for whom intercession is made are overcome. Hence the words of the Most High were most excellently fitting: ﴿until﴾, which is a limit for an expression such as saying: "So when He permits him, there occurs a swooning because of His majesty, His greatness and His perfection, until ﴿when fear is removed﴾, that is, the fear is removed by the easiest matter and the least effort of His command, glorified is He." This is in the reading of the majority, with the passive form. In the reading of Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub, He Himself, glorified is He, removes the fear, indicating that nothing departs from His command. ﴿from their hearts﴾, that is, of the intercessors and those for whom intercession is made. For "fa''ala" comes to denote removal, as in "qadhdhaytu 'aynahu" (I removed the speck from his eye), when you remove the speck from it. ﴿They say﴾, that is, some of them say to others: ﴿What has your Lord said?﴾, mentioning the attribute of goodness so that their hope returns to them and their hearts are thereby at rest.

Since the kings of this world may say a word and then it seems right to them and they retract it, or a person from among the notables of their hosts opposes them in it and it is annulled, He informed that the Sovereign, the Judge, is not like that, so He said: ﴿They say: The truth﴾, that is, the established matter which cannot be altered, but rather reality corresponds to it, so there is nothing that contradicts it. ﴿And He is the Most High﴾, that is, there is no rank except that it is below His rank, glorified and exalted is He, so He does not say other than the truth out of deficiency of knowledge. ﴿the Great﴾, that is, the One than whom there is no greater, so that anyone would oppose Him in any part of a ruling. Al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels strike their wings in submission to His word, like a chain upon smooth rock. ﴿When fear is removed from their hearts, they say: What has your Lord said? They say﴾ (in reply to him who spoke) ﴿the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.﴾ Then the eavesdropper hears it, and the eavesdroppers are thus, one above another," and [he] described it by Sufyan with his hand, bending it and spreading his fingers apart, "so he hears the word and throws it to the one beneath him, then the next throws it to the one beneath him, until it is cast upon the tongue of the sorcerer or the soothsayer. Sometimes the meteor overtakes him before he casts it, and sometimes he casts it before the meteor reaches him, so he lies along with it a hundred lies, and it is said: 'Did he not tell us on such and such a day such and such?' and he is believed because of that one word which was heard from the heaven." In the book of Tawhid, it is also related: Masruq said, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both: "When Allah speaks with the revelation, the inhabitants of the heavens hear it. When fear is removed from their hearts and the sound subsides, they know that it is the truth, and they call out: 'What has your Lord said?' They say: 'The truth.'" [Al-'Ayni also narrated this hadith in his juz' from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, as a statement of his own, saying: "For every group of the jinn there was a seat in the heaven from which they would hear the revelation." And in it: "When it descended to a heaven, they would clap." And at its end: "Then it is said: the year will be such, and the year will be such, and the jinn hear that and inform the soothsayers, who inform the people, and they find it as they said. When Allah sent His Messenger (ﷺ), they were repelled. The Arabs then said: 'The one in the heaven has perished,' and he mentioned the Arabs slaughtering their property of camels and others, until Thaqif forbade them, and they took as evidence the persistence of the star-teachers. Then Iblis ordered his host to bring dust and smell it, until he knew that the event had occurred in Makkah."]

[p. 498] When He had negated from their partners the ability to possess any part of the created existence, and affirmed all sovereignty to Him alone, He commanded him (ﷺ) to make them acknowledge what necessarily follows from that, so He said: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens⁠﴾. Since every aspect of provision depends on the two realms, and this was in the context of bestowing favour and rebuke, He combined them so that it could not be claimed that any being of the higher world has a governor other than Him, glorified is He. So He said: ﴿from the heavens﴾, and He said: ﴿and the earth⁠﴾ in the singular, because they know of no other earth.

Since it was known that they affirm that this belongs to Allah alone, as was stated clearly more than once before, and since it is established that their affirmation of this obliges them to sincerity in worship in the view of everyone who has even a little sense, He indicated this by commanding him (ﷺ) to answer, implying that they are like those who deny this, because their affirmation of it did not benefit them. So He said: ﴿Say: Allah⁠﴾, that is, [the Supreme King] alone. And after establishing this clear proof, He commanded him to follow it with what is more painful to them than the impact of arrows, in a manner that is wholly just, and no one could direct any kind of criticism at it. He said, emphatically, alerting them to the necessity of thoroughly examining the distinction between the true and the false by freeing oneself from desire, since the matter is of the utmost gravity: ﴿And indeed we or you⁠﴾, that is, we, the people of monotheism in worship, toward the One who alone provides, or you, the people of associating others with Him, who possess nothing of things. [p. 499] The "or" here is used in its proper sense and not in the sense of "and." That is, one of the two parties is in one of two states, which is left indefinite and unspecified, so he is in great danger, since he is in doubt about his matter and is not certain of guidance. So consider with your minds which of the two it is: is it the one who recognised the truth for its people, or the one who gave the truth to those who are not its people?

Ibn al-Jawzi said: This is like saying to a man whom you are accusing: "By God, one of us is surely a liar," while you mean a denial that is not openly stated. And a man says: "By God, so-and-so has arrived," and someone who knows that he is lying says to him: "Say, if God wills," thereby denying him in a manner better than a plain denial. That is, especially after the establishment of the proof for the intended meaning.

Then he likened the guided to someone riding a steed, who directs it wherever he wishes, with His words: ﴿surely upon guidance⁠﴾, that is, in following what one should do, standing over it, watchful of everything that might present itself in it and might lead to error, so that one avoids it. ﴿Or in error⁠﴾, [that is,] away from the truth in the appropriate belief, immersed in it, and it encompasses the one afflicted by it, leaving him no way to correctness: ﴿clear⁠﴾, that is, evident in itself, calling everyone to recognise that it is error, except for one who is immersed in it and enclosed by it, for he does not perceive himself, nor what lies between him and gaining insight, unless he comes out of it at some point and knows that in that state he was doing what no one with any degree of intellect would do. [p. 500] In this there is an exhortation to the reflection that they used to refuse, with His words: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings⁠﴾ [Fussilat: 5], and similar. It is in the proofs by which truth is distinguished from falsehood in the best manner, with the most just invitation and the gentlest call, in that the one calling includes himself with them in what he invites them to examine. The meaning is that it is incumbent upon each of us, when we are on one of two paths, while it is unspecified which, to examine the matter so that he may be safe, for the matter is in the utmost clarity, even though the one who is astray is in the greatest danger.

The distinguished Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and those of sound judgement and understanding among them, used to say this after embracing Islam, such as Khalid ibn al-Walid and Amr ibn al-As, and sufficient are these two in nobility, intelligence, shrewdness and perfection. They said: "By God, we used to wonder to the utmost degree at the one who entered Islam, and today we wonder to the utmost degree at the one who hesitates to embrace it."

When they were between two options, either to remain silent, so that every listener would know that the proof had bound them, or to say with impudence and obstinacy, "You are in error and we are upon guidance," and the one astray keeps cutting what should be joined, by joining what must be cut, He commanded him (the Prophet) to answer them on this assumption with what is more equitable than the first, by His saying: ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we have committed﴾, that is, from any questioner, regarding what we have committed, that is, what we have cut off in it of what should have been joined, from what error has made incumbent upon us, ﴿and we will not be asked﴾, that is, at all, at any time, [by any questioner] ﴿about what you do﴾, that is, of what you have built upon the knowledge that guidance has bequeathed to you. That is: leave us and the people other than yourselves, just as we are leaving you. Whoever finds any of the two paths clear to him, let him follow it.

Since they were either going to accept the proposal of leaving one another alone, whereby they would soon attain their aim, or else say, "We will not leave you," and this latter possibility was more likely, He commanded him to answer them on that assumption with His words: ﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together﴾, that is, in His judgment, which is ordered according to His decree in this world or in the Hereafter. Al-Qushayri said: "The shaykhs await gatherings (al-ijtima') with great anticipation and find solace in this verse, and gathering (al-ijtima') holds a great matter in the Sharia."

Since their being fair to one another was extremely remote in their view, and since that (fairness) is in itself extremely great, He indicated it with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿Then He will open﴾, that is, He will judge ﴿between us﴾ with a judgment by which the path becomes easy, ﴿with truth﴾, that is, with the established matter from which neither any one of us nor any of you can deviate, and it is justice or grace without injustice or partiality. Since the implied meaning is: "So He is the All-Gatherer, the All-Powerful," He followed it with His words: ﴿And He is the Opener﴾, that is, the one who opens thoroughly what has been closed, so that no one can open it except Him, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the one who thoroughly carries out, with every subtle and grand detail, all that in which judgments may take place. Thus He is the One Able to decide all disputes.

When they had denied the resurrection in the manner already mentioned, and He had shown His power over it through the proofs He set up, which they witnessed with their eyes or their insight, in bringing things into existence and annihilating them, and He had established the proof for the soundness of the call and the falsehood of what they held, then He threatened them with the decisive judgment on the Day of Assembly, and concluded with the attribute of all-encompassing knowledge, which entails comprehensive power. Since power cannot be comprehensive except with oneness, He commanded him to say what necessitates for them certainty of His oneness and the comprehensiveness of His power, with His words: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these polytheists.

Since their gods are visible, and everything that is like that is of lowly rank compared to this station, and their gods in particular are the lowest of things in this respect, being among the most base inanimate objects, He drew attention to this and to the fact that they are unknown, that no heart recognizes them and no natural disposition points to them, as an added rebuke to them, with His words: ﴿Show me those whom﴾. When what is established for Him, glorified be He, of attributes of perfection and [exaltedness] that no one can approach in any respect is necessarily entailed, He said: ﴿you have joined with Him﴾. Since joining necessarily implies the inferiority of what is joined compared to that to which it is joined, He pointed to the extreme of their ignorance in equating them with Him, with His words: ﴿as partners﴾. Then, after refuting their analogy, He alerted them, since they are in the utmost coarseness and rigidity, and so are like cattle, with the reproach He directed at them, emphasizing the denial of their claim of association, in His words: ﴿Nay﴾, that is, refrain and desist. The matter is not as you have mentioned, by Allah, nor anything close to it. ﴿Rather, He﴾, that is, the one truly worshipped, who does not deserve that anything else be named by it, ﴿is Allah﴾, that is, the One specially deserving of praise in this world and the next, ﴿the Almighty﴾, that is, the One who has no like, and everything is in need of Him, and He prevails over everything with a dominance such that the thing finds no way to resist or reverse it, and nothing reaches Him except by His permission, ﴿the All-Wise﴾, that is, the One who perfects everything He does, so no one can undo any part of it. How then could He have a partner, when you see in Him these two attributes that negate it, and you know the incapacity of the one you have associated with Him to equal you, along with what you know of your own incapacity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 28:

When he concluded with the description of wisdom, the proof of power was complete, the power whose affirmation, for the sake of denying resurrection, they had been compelled to hold by something that requires a deficiency in it. And from that arose monotheism, and polytheism was nullified. Nothing remained but the affirmation of the prophethood, for which their repeated rejection of his ﷺ reports, between lying, madness and disparagement of it, had necessitated it. It is known, then, that the sense is: He sent to you His Messenger, by His might, supporting him with the miraculous inimitability of this Qur'an, by His wisdom, as proof of his truthfulness, his perfection in his nature, and his fitness for the marvels of His blessing and the lofty heights of His mercy. In this was the proof of truthfulness in the prophethood. So He linked to it His saying, exalting his rank by addressing him in the manifestation of greatness, as an indication that he should wrap himself in the garments of patience against all the hardships coming from various kinds of creatures in the performance of the message, with His saying, conjoined to ﴿And We had certainly given David bounty from Us﴾ [Saba': 10], emphatically refuting those who claim exclusivity: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾, i.e., by Our greatness, ﴿except comprehensively﴾, i.e., a general sending encompassing everything that Our creation encompasses, restraining them from what they might otherwise be inclined to spread toward, from following desires, and preventing any of them from going out of it. So the ta' in "kaffatan" is for emphasis. The expression of Ibn al-Jawzi: i.e., general for all creation. ﴿to mankind﴾, i.e., every one of whom there is capacity to be warned, of the jinn and mankind and others, from all that is other than Allah, ﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. And even if they harm you with every kind of harm, such as attributing to you fabrication or madness or other things. Thus the state of sending is restricted to generality for the purpose mentioned, namely the bearing of hardships, not restricted to mankind; for had that been intended, they would have been placed first, and it would have said: "except for mankind, comprehensively." (p-505) Al-Subki's remarks at the beginning of al-An'am, which are useful here, have already passed. The meaning is that David, peace be upon him, was favored by the mountains obeying him, and the birds and iron, and Solomon, peace be upon him, by what is mentioned for him. Your excellence, then, is by being sent to everyone who is capable of being warned. The pebbles glorified in your palm, the mountains were commanded to travel with you, gold and silver [were given to you], the female wild ass complained to you about the taking of her young or her eggs, the lizard bore witness for you, the camel complained to you and prostrated to you, the trees obeyed you, the stones greeted you and submitted to your command, and so on for everyone who is warned in actuality or in capacity. And Allah knows best. As for the jinn, their situation is well known. As for the angels, the proofs of sending to them are most evident. [And in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, in the chapter on speaking of blessings, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that this verse is evidence of the superiority of the Prophet ﷺ over the prophets, by the generality of his message to mankind and the jinn.]

Since good tidings is the first true report that gladdens, and since mentioning it refutes their saying of lying and madness, He said: ﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾, i.e., to whoever is fit for good tidings or warning. Since this sending was accompanied by its proof, namely the bringing of a miracle from himself, through the eloquence of its composition and through the firm meanings in good tidings and warning and other things, He turned against them their saying, which has no proof and no doubt that can be aimed at him ﷺ, with a saying that [is] clearer than the sun as proof and most upright of every saying in speech: ﴿But﴾. And since the earliest people were every one in whom there is capacity to be warned, and they are all creation, and most of them [are not] disobedient, He made apparent that He intends the two weights, the jinn and mankind, and said: ﴿most of mankind do not know﴾, i.e., they do not have the capacity for knowledge so that they would know you are the Messenger of Allah, let alone that your sending is general. Rather they are like livestock, and so they do not reflect, and say "He has fabricated it, or is there madness in him?" and similar things, without contemplating what is in this Book of wisdom and rightness, together with inimitability in both its concision and its expansiveness, its concealment and its disclosure. Their ignorance thus drives them to opposition and turning away.

Having removed knowledge from them, He followed it with its evidence, saying, using the present-tense form that indicates the continuous recurrence of the act, to inform that this is by way of mockery and not of seeking guidance: ﴿And they say﴾, meaning: "You (Muhammad) were not sent except in this state," while the state is that the warners say, out of their ignorance of the outcome of what they are threatened with, not reflecting upon how to escape from it and be free of it, at every moment, in mockery from them: ﴿When is this promise?﴾, meaning: the promise of good tidings and warning on the Day of Assembly and other times. They called it a "promise" in addition to the mockery.

Since the speech of a group is more worthy of acceptance and further from rejection than the speech of one individual, he pointed to the increase of their ignorance by saying: ﴿If you are﴾, meaning: O Prophet and those who follow you, being firmly established in it, ﴿truthful﴾, [meaning] those who are firmly established in truthfulness.

Now that it has become clear from their questioning that they did not ask for guidance, and that even though they persisted in denial and mockery after the proofs had been fully presented, He commanded him to answer them with what suits the stubborn: a piercing threat, by His saying: ﴿Say: "For you is an appointment of a day"﴾ — that is, O you rigid, coarse ones who do not admit what is possible and do not reflect upon the clear indications that made it plain, despite their weakness in defense, their exaggeration, and their refusal. ﴿An appointment of a day﴾ — that is, the intellects cannot bear to describe its greatness, because of the punishment that will come in it, whether it is the day of death or the day of resurrection. And since the souls' attachment to a respite is great, He said: ﴿You will not delay from it﴾ — that is, your delay cannot be found, nor can it be sought, given the urgent pursuit and the impossibility of escape, ﴿for an hour﴾, because the One who brings it is of great power and encompassing knowledge. For this reason He said: ﴿nor will you advance [it]﴾ — that is, your advancing cannot be found for a moment or less, nor can you be able to seek that.

ولَمّا دَلَّ سُبْحانَهُ بِمُلازَمَتِهِمْ لِلِاسْتِهْزاءِ بِهَذا الإنْذارِ عَلى أنَّهم غَيْرُ (p-٥٠٨)مُنْفَكِّينَ عَنْ مَذاهِبِ الكُفّارِ، ذَكَرَ تَصْرِيحَهم بِذَلِكَ وحالَهم في بَعْضِ الأوْقاتِ المُنْطَبِقَةِ عَلَيْها الآيَةُ السّالِفَةُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ حَيْثُ عَبَّرَ بِالمَوْصُولِ وصِلَتِهِ في مَوْضِعِ الضَّمِيرِ، قَطْعًا لِلْأطْماعِ عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ﴾ أيْ نُصَدِّقَ أبَدًا، وصَرَّحُوا بِالمُنْزَلِ عَلَيْهِ (ﷺ) بِالإشارَةِ فَقالُوا: ﴿بِهَذا القُرْآنِ﴾ أيْ وإنْ جَمَعَ جَمِيعَ الحِكَمِ والمَقاصِدِ المُضَمَّنَةِ لِبَقِيَّةِ الكُتُبِ ﴿ولا بِالَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ أيْ قَبْلَهُ مِنَ الكُتُبِ: التَّوْراةُ والإنْجِيلُ وغَيْرُهُما. بَلْ نَحْنُ قانِعُونَ بِما أدَّبَنا بِهِ آباؤُنا، وذَلِكَ أنَّ بَعْضَ أهْلِ الكِتابِ أخْبَرُوهم أنَّ صِفَةَ هَذا النَّبِيِّ عِنْدَهم في كُتُبِهِمْ، فَأغْضَبَهم ذَلِكَ فَقالُوهُ: ﴿ولَوْ﴾ أيْ والحالُ أنَّكَ ﴿تَرى﴾ أيْ يُوجَدُ مِنكَ رُؤْيَةٌ لِحالِهِمْ ﴿إذِ﴾ هم - هَكَذا كانَ الأصْلُ - ولَكِنْ أظْهَرَ الوَصْفَ تَعْمِيمًا وتَعْلِيقًا لِلْحُكْمِ بِهِ فَقالَ: ﴿الظّالِمُونَ﴾ أيِ الَّذِينَ يَضَعُونَ الأشْياءَ في غَيْرِ مَحالِّها فَيُصَدِّقُونَ آباءَهم لِإحْسانٍ يَسِيرٍ مُكَدَّرٍ بِغَيْرِ دَلِيلٍ، ولا يُصَدِّقُونَ رَبَّهُمُ الَّذِي لا نِعْمَةَ عِنْدَهم ولا عِنْدَ آبائِهِمْ إلّا مِنهُ، وقَدْ أقامَ لَهم أدِلَّةَ العَقْلِ بِما ضَرَبَ لَهم مِنَ الأمْثالِ في الآفاقِ وفي أنْفُسِهِمْ، والنَّقْلُ بِهَذا القُرْآنِ (p-٥٠٩)المَدْلُولِ عَلى صِدْقِهِ بَعْدَ إظْهارِ المُعْجِزاتِ المَحْسُوساتِ [بِعَجْزِهِمْ عَنْهُ، فَكَأنَّهم سَمِعُوهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ المُنْعِمِ الحَقِّ ﴿مَوْقُوفُونَ﴾ أيْ بَعْدَ البَعْثِ بِما يُوقِفُهم مِن قُدْرَتِهِ بِأيْدِي جُنُودِهِ أوْ بِغَيْرِها] بِأيْسَرِ أمْرٍ مِنهُ سُبْحانَهُ قَهْرًا لَهم وكَرْهًا مِنهُمْ: ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ أيِ الَّذِي أحْسَنَ إلَيْهِمْ فَطالَ إحْسانُهُ فَكَفَرُوا كُلَّما أحْسَنَ بِهِ إلَيْهِمْ ﴿يَرْجِعُ بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ أيْ عَلى وجْهِ الخِصامِ عَداوَةً، [و] كانَ سَبَبُها مُوادَدَتَهم في الدُّنْيا بِطاعَةِ بَعْضِهِمْ لِبَعْضٍ في مَعاصِي اللَّهِ، قالَ القُشَيْرِيُّ: ومَن عَمِلَ بِالمَعاصِي أخْرَجَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ كُلَّ مَن هو أطْوَعُ لَهُ، ولَكِنَّهم لا يَعْلَمُونَ ذَلِكَ، ولَوْ عَلِمُوا لاعْتَبَرُوا، ولَوِ اعْتَبَرُوا لَتابُوا وتَوافَقُوا، ولَكِنْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أمْرًا كانَ مَفْعُولًا ﴿إلى بَعْضٍ القَوْلَ﴾ أيْ بِالمُلاوَمَةِ والمُباكَتَةِ والمُخاصَمَةِ، لَرَأيْتَ أمْرًا فَظِيعًا مُنْكَرًا هائِلًا شَنِيعًا مُقْلِقًا وجِيعًا يَسُرُّكَ مَنظَرُهُ، ويُعْجِبُكَ مِنهم أثَرُهُ ومَخْبَرُهُ، مِن ذُلِّهِمْ وتَحاوُرِهِمْ وتَخاذُلِهِمْ حَيْثُ لا يَنْفَعُهم شَيْءٌ مِن ذَلِكَ.

ولَمّا كانَ هَذا مُجْمَلًا، فَسَّرَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ عَلى سَبِيلِ الِاسْتِئْنافِ (isti'naf: resumptive, a new sentence introduced to explain what precedes): ﴿يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا﴾ أيْ وقَعَ اسْتِضْعافُهم مِمَّنْ هو فَوْقَهم في الدُّنْيا وهُمُ الأتْباعُ في تِلْكَ الحالَةِ عَلى سَبِيلِ اللَّوْمِ والتَّأْنِيبِ ﴿لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ أيْ أوْجَدُوا الكِبْرَ وطَلَبُوهُ بِما وجَدُوا مِن أسْبابِهِ الَّتِي أدَّتْ إلى اسْتِضْعافِهِمْ (p-٥١٠)لِلْأوَّلِينَ وهُمُ الرُّؤُوسُ المَتْبُوعُونَ: ﴿لَوْلا أنْتُمْ﴾ أيْ مِمّا وُجِدَ مِنِ اسْتِتْباعِكم لَنا عَلى الكُفْرِ وغَيْرِهِ مِن أُمُورِكم ﴿لَكُنّا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ أيْ عَرِيقَيْنِ في الإيمانِ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَنا كَبْرٌ مِن أنْفُسِنا يَحْمِلُنا عَلى العِنادِ لِلرُّسُلِ.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 32:

When their speech contained only one proposition, he mentioned the response with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾ by way of resumption (isti'naf), ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾, as a rejection of them and a denial of their claim that they were the ones who barred them, ﴿Did we bar you﴾ — ﴿we﴾ specifically — ﴿from guidance﴾, meaning, we prevented you and turned you away ﴿from guidance, after it had come to you﴾, meaning through the tongues of the messengers. And since they were not held accountable for neglecting the evidence of reason before the coming of the messengers, they alluded to that by their saying: ﴿after it had come to you﴾.

And since the meaning was: "We did not do that," it was fitting to say that they themselves were the ones who went astray by their own selves, not by being led astray by others. So they said: ﴿Rather, you were﴾, meaning by nature and by creation, ﴿criminals﴾, meaning persistent in severing what ought to be joined after the coming of guidance, choosing that willingly, just as you were before it, followers of us; you did not refuse, nor did we.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 33:

Since their statement contained two matters, the claim of their being rooted in criminality (ʿarāqa fī al-ijrām) and the denial that they were the cause of it, he pointed to their rebuttal of the second by using the conjunction (al-ʿāṭif) without anything preceding it to be conjoined to, to make known that the implied sense is: "Those who were oppressed said: You lie in what you claimed of our being rooted in criminality." ﴿And those who were oppressed said﴾, conjoined to this implied statement, ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾, in rebuttal of their denial that they had barred them (p-511): ﴿Nay, [it was] the plotting of the night and the day﴾ — that is, the plotting that took place in them from your scheming against us — or the attribution of plotting to them was used figuratively because of the long duration of safety in them; and this is for the expansiveness of the temporal noun in treating it as the object. ﴿When you commanded us﴾ continuously ﴿to disbelieve in God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, by persisting in what we were upon before the coming of the messengers, ﴿and to set up rivals to Him﴾, that is, equals whom we worship besides Him. ﴿And they concealed﴾, that is, they returned, while the two groups were in fact concealing ﴿the regret when﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿they saw the punishment﴾. This is because, while they were in that dispute, thinking that it would avail them something, suddenly there appeared to them what they had not been expecting, which bewildered them; so they were unable, due to the loss of their aims and the ruin of their souls, to utter a single word. And because the punishment encompassed both the noble among them and the lowly. God Most High said: ﴿And We placed the shackles﴾, that is, the collars that bind the hand to the neck, ﴿upon the necks of those who disbelieved﴾. Here the place of the pronoun was replaced by the explicit noun, to state the intended meaning clearly and to draw attention to the attribute that necessitated this for them.

Since their deeds, because of their ugliness, call for disavowal of them, and since by their constant adherence to them it was as if these deeds had overpowered them into persisting in them and wearing them like the collar of the dove [so they stubbornly oppose the truth without turning to any evidence], He said, drawing attention to this, in answer to one who seems to have said: Why were their necks and hands singled out for this punishment?: ﴿Are they recompensed﴾, that is, with these shackles, ﴿except for what they used to be﴾, that is, in a state in which they were steeped, ﴿doing﴾, that is, in a manner of continual renewal and persistence, of what they claim they founded upon knowledge. And that recompense — God knows best — is what necessitates their subjugation, humiliation, disgrace, injury, and pain, just as they used to do with the believers and wished for them.

When this contained an otherworldly consolation, he followed it with a worldly consolation. He said, coordinating with what its implied meaning is: "We did not send any warner before you except as a special sending to his community," coordinated with ﴿We did not send you except comprehensively﴾ [Saba': 28]. He stated it with emphasis because its content, being extremely strange, is something that can hardly be believed: ﴿We did not send﴾, i.e., by Our greatness. Since the intent is generality, and the statement of Quraysh had not preceded to restrict the consolation to those before them, he dropped the "before" (qabliyyah), unlike what is in Surat al-Zukhruf. So he said: ﴿in a town﴾. He emphasized the negation with his saying: ﴿any warner﴾, i.e., one who warns them of the ill-end of what lies ahead of them, of those who were punished for their deeds. By singling out warning and not good tidings, he indicates that most of the past nations were people of warning, so that the distinction of this nation would be manifest. Perhaps he expressed it this way as an allusion to the abrogators of the laws before them, not the renewers from the prophets of the Children of Israel, for some of them (p-513) were not denied. ﴿Except that its affluent ones said﴾, i.e., the great ones who have no concern except enjoying the fleeting world, until indulgence and transgression earned them: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾, i.e., O warners. ﴿Disbelieve﴾: that is, when the affluent said that, the weak followed them. Then when they stood before Us, they blamed one another with what has been mentioned before.

Then that did not benefit them. "And they said," boasting and indicating that they are the successful ones, [as] these people said to you, as if they had agreed upon it: "We have more..."

Since wealth was generally the cause of having many children, through taking many free women and slave women, he mentioned it first, saying: "wealth and children" — that is, in this world. Had He not been pleased with what we are upon, He would not have granted us this. "And we are not" — that is, now — "punished," meaning our punishment is not established. Rather, there come upon us light conditions of sickness and hardships that are lighter than your conditions. Our present state is a proof of our state in what is yet to come of time, whatever it may be, for the present state is the model of the outcome, and the first is a proof of the last. So if there is an Hereafter, as you say, then we will be happier than you in it, just as we are happier than you now. The story of Saba' did not benefit them in this, for if they had reflected it would have sufficed them, and it would have illuminated the insight of their hearts and healed the diseases of their hearts and their souls, for they were the best of people in condition, and they became the worst of them in outcome.

(p-514) Since their doubt had two branches, one concerning the essence (of the matter) and the other concerning the fruits, he began with the first because it is more important. So he said, emphatically, refuting those who think that their striving benefits them in provision, and that without striving it would not have come about: ﴿Say﴾, O most noble of creation before God! Emphasized because of their denial that He should expand the world for one whose deeds He does not approve: ﴿Indeed, my Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to me by bestowing eternal happiness, ﴿extends provision﴾, that is, renews it at every time He wills, with wealth, children and other things, ﴿for whom He wills and restricts [it]﴾, that is, He restricts it for whom He wills among you, among us, and among others from all the nations that oppose us and you in the fundamentals. [Yet] it is not possible that all those for whom He expands (provision) are upon what is true and pleasing to Him, due to their disagreement in the fundamentals and their declaring one another to be unbelievers; for God will surely punish some of them. Thus their doubt is refuted, and it is established that He does what He wills as a trial and test, so expansion does not indicate approval, nor restriction indicate displeasure, according to what is known of His practice in this abode. ﴿But most people﴾, that is, those who have not risen above the level of wavering and agitation, ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge by which they might reflect upon what we have mentioned of the matter, so that they would know that not everyone who is expanded upon in his worldly life is happy in his final end.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 34, verse 37:

When he (Allah) had demolished what pertains to the essence (of the claim), He followed it with what pertains to the fruits (of wealth and children). So He said, emphasizing the refutation of their claim: ﴿And neither your wealth nor your children﴾, that is, O creatures, you who are among their number, however many they may be. He repeated the negation to make explicit the nullification of each separately, so He said: ﴿nor your children﴾ likewise. He retained the preposition (bi) to emphasize the negation, and He said, describing the broken plural with what is its due feminine form: ﴿except those which﴾, that is, the wealth and children which ﴿bring you near to Us﴾, that is, in accordance with our greatness, through your dealings with them in ways that gain lofty ranks, ﴿in nearness﴾, that is, an exalted degree and a firmly established closeness. Al-Baghawi said: Al-Akhfash said: it is an infinitive of the form (ism masdar), as if he said: "bringing near" (taqrib). Then He made an exception from the pronoun of the plural, which stands in place of someone (aḥad), as if it were said: "Do not bring anyone near, ﴿except for him who﴾. Or the meaning is with an elided modifier, that is, except the wealth and children of him who ﴿believes﴾, that is, among you, ﴿and does﴾ righteous deeds confirming his faith on that foundation, ﴿righteous﴾, that is, with his wealth by spending it in the way of Allah, and with his child by teaching him good.

When He had bestowed favor upon the righteous among the believers regarding their wealth and children, by making them a means of greater nearness for them, He indicated this with the fa' in His saying: ﴿So those﴾ (p-516), that is, those of elevated rank, ﴿will have the recompense of double﴾, that is, they will receive their reward multiplied, in itself from ten times to an endless extent, and multiplied in comparison with the reward of those who came before them among the nations. And "ḍi'f" (double) means increase. ﴿for what they did﴾, for their deeds are established and preserved on the foundation of faith. ﴿And they will be in the lofty chambers﴾, that is, the elevated structures built above the houses in the gardens, in addition to that, ﴿secure﴾, that is, their security is permanently established, with no fear upon them from any thing whatsoever. As for others, who are the intended ones in what follows, their wealth and children are a burden upon them.

When the context was one of encouraging faith, after the announcement that he is a bringer of good news and a warner, He said, using the present tense to explain the state of those whom their wealth and children keep far from God: ﴿And those who strive﴾, meaning they continually renew their striving without repentance, with their wealth and their children, ﴿against Our signs﴾, in light of the great honor of their being attributed to Us, ﴿seeking to frustrate [them]﴾, meaning seeking to render them powerless, that is, to render powerless those who bring them, so that they fail to carry out their purposes through them, by casting the doubts they cast, thereby misleading others, by means of the wealth and children with which We have expanded for them and strengthened them.

Since He, glorified is He, had decided their wretchedness and carried out the decree of their loss, He dropped the fā' of causation (fāʾ al-sabab, the "fa" that marks a consequence) out of disregard for their deeds and said: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the distant (p-517) and hateful, ﴿are in the punishment﴾, meaning the one that removes sweetness, ﴿brought forth﴾, meaning those who are assigned to them from Our hosts will bring them forth to it in the easiest and gentlest manner, while they are abased. Al-Qushayri said: These are the ones who do not honor the awliyāʾ (friends of God) and do not observe the right of God in secret. So they are in the punishment of opposing the friends of God, and in the punishment of falling, through the evil consequence of that, into the violation of God's prohibitions, and then in the punishment of being cast down from the sight of God.

When he had refuted their doubt in both of its branches, with respect to the different individuals, he brought this closer through a single proof concerning a single person, saying: ﴿Say﴾ O most noble of creation, to these ignorant people who suppose that provision depends on the goodness or badness of one's striving, or on the good or bad state of the person in the sight of Allah: ﴿Indeed my Lord﴾ [i.e., the One who has favoured me with this inimitable exposition] ﴿extends provision﴾, i.e., whenever He wills, ﴿to whomever He wills of His servants﴾, i.e., in a continual, ongoing manner, from whatever group he may be, ﴿and restricts it for him﴾, i.e., He constricts it upon him, in two alternating states, while he is in one and the same condition, performing one and the same action. Had honour and bounty required permanence, his state would not have changed from abundance to constriction. And had the power to benefit oneself been in one's own hand, his condition would not have varied.

When this extension made clear that His act is by choice, after he had first shown their falsehood in claiming that spending is a cause of safety from the Fire, he then indicated, through His saying, that He alone is the one who acts and no other: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything﴾, i.e., you, your adversaries, and others besides, ﴿He will replace it﴾ (p. 518) i.e., it is not anyone else, as evidenced by the fact that the one who spends may strive with all his effort to avoid replacement and so not spend. This shows that He is the one exclusively entrusted with replacement. Moreover, this is the meaning, not that He has guaranteed replacement for everyone who spends in whatever manner. Mujahid said, as al-Razi transmitted it in al-Lawami': "If there is something in the hand of one of you, let him be moderate and not interpret the verse, for provision is apportioned, and whoever is moderate does not fall into poverty." This was narrated by al-Tabarani from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, in a marfu' report. The meaning is that replacement, in all its forms and opposites, has shown that the matter in it is other than what you supposed, namely that it is an assistance given at a time that necessitates continual honour. Rather, that is only because of His guarantee of provision to each person according to what He has apportioned to him, in accordance with what His knowledge, power and wisdom have preceded. Sometimes His replacement is sensory and actual, and sometimes it is in meaning and potential, through contentment with that state which led to nonexistence. Al-Qushayri said: "This is more complete than joy in what exists. Among this is intimacy with Allah in solitude, and this is only found together with tajrid (detachment from all but Allah)." End of quotation. The one who spends with moderation is included, God willing, under His ﷺ saying, which al-Bukhari and Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said that Allah the Exalted said: "Spend, and I will spend upon you." And what al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih also related: "There is not a morning on which the servants rise but two angels descend, one of them saying: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement,' and the other (p. 519) saying: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.'" So He is the best of those who bestow. ﴿And He is the best of providers﴾, i.e., those whom you reckon in this category as being provided for by Him, through whom you attribute provision to them. For they are intermediaries who are able only to do what He has empowered them to do. As for Him, glory be to Him, He brings the non-existent into existence, provides for those who obey Him and those who disobey Him, and His provision is not constricted for anyone, nor does giving to one occupy Him from another. Rather, He sends to each person, every day, his provision in a single instant, just as He spreads over them His light through the sun in a single instant, without that being restricted to anything other than what knowledge has preceded from eternity.
