When He had refuted their doubt, and it became known from this that the whole affair belongs to Him alone, and that they are in a place of danger, and there remained among their doubts their saying, "We worship the angels, so they intercede for us," and the prophets, peace be upon them, did not deny that the angels are the closely-held ones (muqarrabun), He refuted what they clung to of them and made clear that they have no authority, and that they are free of them. So He said, conjoining it to ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾ [Saba': 31], ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them﴾, meaning, We will assemble them in a gathering, by compulsion, after the resurrection, and He included the follower and the followed with His words: ﴿all together﴾.

Since the stations of the gathering are long and its convulsions terrifying, He said: ﴿Then He will say to the angels﴾, meaning, as a rebuke to the polytheists and to make them despair of the intercession they hoped to receive from them. And since worship does not benefit unless the one worshipped is pleased with it and it is sincere, He said, reproving the polytheists and rebuking them, so that there would be a question and an answer (p-520), so that the reproach would be more severe, the shame greater, and the fear and humiliation more complete and more binding, and so that the recounting of this would be an admonition to the listeners, a deterrent to the ignorant, and a warning to the heedless, in the manner of ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116] and the following verses: ﴿These﴾, meaning the erring ones; and he indicated that nothing of worship benefits except what is sincere, so He said: ﴿They used to worship you﴾, meaning you alone, ﴿through their voluntary and compelled acts﴾, so that it would be known that they are your servants, whom you deserve to be worshipped, and in the use of an expression that indicates exclusivity (ikhtisas) there is a warning to the Quraysh that nothing of worship is counted except what is purely sincere.

﴿They say﴾, that is, the angels, disavowing them, beginning with glorification, humbling themselves before the disavowal, out of fear of the descent of punishment: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, we glorify You with a glorification befitting Your majesty, [so that] none other than You deserves to be worshipped.

Since they were utterly averse to their worship, and since the benefit of worship is the connection between the worshipper and the worshipped, they said: ﴿You are our protector﴾, that is, our Worshipped One, with whom there is no connection between us and anyone except by His command, ﴿rather than them﴾ [that is, You are nearer to us than their position in relation to us, for You are nearer to us than anything in every sense of protection, such as knowledge, power and other things. How then could we abandon the Nearest and the Most Powerful and turn to the most distant and the powerless?], there is no protection between us and them, but rather enmity. Likewise, everyone who draws near to a person by disobeying God, God hardens his heart against him, makes him hate him for it, so he shuns him and becomes hostile to him.

Since whoever works for someone a work that he did not command and did not approve, in reality works for the One who called him to that work, they said: ﴿Rather, they used to worship﴾ through their voluntary actions which necessitate association (shirk), ﴿the jinn﴾, that is, Iblis and his offspring, who adorned for them the worship of us without our approval [of that]. They used to enter into the bellies of the idols, address them, and seek refuge with them in frightening places. From this is the saying: «Woe to the servant of the dinar, the servant of the dirham, and the servant of the velvet cloak.» Then they resumed their statement: ﴿Most of them﴾, that is, humankind, ﴿believe in them﴾, that is, the jinn, ﴿[are] believers﴾, that is, firmly established in association, not intending by their worship anything other than them. And a few of them intend by their worship the adornment of the jinn and others, and he is content with it; so it is in reality for the one among the jinn who adorned it for them. Yet, along with that, they accept what reaches them of the reports of the jinn through the tongues of soothsayers (kuhhan) and others, even though they see in them much falsehood at many times.

When their clinging to claims was nullified and their attachments were severed, there followed from that their rebuke, which resulted in their regret, expressed in the words of (God's) majestic voice: ﴿So today﴾, that is, the day of their being addressed with this reproach, which is the Day of Gathering, ﴿none of you has power﴾ [i.e.] over any part of dominion ﴿for another﴾, that is, of those brought near and those removed far. Since the matter revolves around deliverance and the context concerns intercession, he put benefit first, saying ﴿benefit﴾, and completed the matter with His words ﴿nor harm﴾, as a confirmation of severing all the means that existed in the abode of obligation, (so as to reach) the abode of recompense, in which the purpose is the full manifestation of greatness to God alone in the most perfect aspects.

Since the meaning is: "So today We strip the creatures of what We had empowered them with in the world, of mutual benefit and mutual harm," and everything other than Him vanished thereby, He affirmed for His holy self what is fitting, saying, conjoining it to what I have estimated: ﴿And We will say﴾, that is, in that state, without delay or neglect, ﴿to those who did wrong﴾, that is, by placing worship in other than its proper place, especially whoever added to that the denial of the Return when We cause them to enter the Fire: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire﴾. And since no description had preceded for the punishment with a qualifier of repetition, as preceded in the prostration (surah), nor otherwise, the annexed noun [ilayhi] was more deserving of the description, because it is the object directed at with denial. So He said: ﴿which you used to﴾, that is, by innate disposition and nature, ﴿deny﴾.

[p. 523] When He informed them that they refused to believe in the Qur'an, the one that gives news of the unseen from the command of the Most Merciful, the One to whom minds have been guided and whose signs eyes have witnessed, in this inimitable speech, the proofs of hearing, sight and reason converged on what it reported. He concluded by [informing] that they believed in the jinn as unseen beings and worshipped them besides Allah, for which neither reason nor transmission calls. They also believed what the jinn told them, and when those reports were true in any part, they mixed with it more than a hundred lies. He negated from the greatest of those whom they claimed they relied upon the power to benefit and to harm, and He attributed their punishment to their denial. Then He followed this with the report that they persisted in that disbelief and denial, though all of it is truth and wisdom. So He said: ﴿And when Our signs are recited﴾, that is, at any time, by whichever reciter it may be, ﴿to them﴾ [that is, specifically, not shared with others, so that they could not say: it was meant for someone else in the recitation, and so hearing it would not be binding on them], ﴿clear signs﴾ being such that whatever they say, its truth becomes evident, ﴿they say﴾ [that is, immediately, without reflection, because of the self's share (of desire) that moved them to this].

When the arrogant saw the prominence of the Message and the acceptance of the Messenger, and that their followers had come to see this, they inclined toward it wholeheartedly. Their statement emphasized it: ﴿This is not﴾ [that is] the one reciting it, despite its bearing that marks him as the most truthful of creation, the most lofty in aspiration and the clearest in counsel, ﴿except a man﴾, that is, although he is one, he is like any one of your men, and you outnumber him in multitude. [They did not attribute the action to themselves, to negate the purpose from themselves and to incite the addressees], ﴿He wants to turn you﴾, that is, by this which he recites, ﴿away from what your fathers used to worship﴾ [always], that is, he has no aim but that, so that you become his followers. They inflamed the listeners by portraying their fathers, using "used to" (kāna) and the present-tense verb, as constantly devoted to worship, so that they would remain upon their disbelief with what has no evidence, no basis, and no motive except imitation.

When the proofs of the Book were clear, they feared its consequence on accepting it, so they firmly declared it to be a lie, in order to hold them back by this. Allah the Glorified related this about them in His saying: ﴿And they said, "This is not﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿except a fabrication﴾, that is, a lie turned away from its true course, ﴿invented﴾, that is, deliberately made up, with what is in it of distortion.

When it contained what no one doubts in its truth, they confused them by claiming it was an imagination that would soon be exposed, to hold them back for some time. So the Exalted said, reporting about them: ﴿And said﴾. Since truth may be hidden, and He did not restrict it with clarity as He did with the verses, He stated the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, to make clear the attribute that moved them to that statement, which is deception. So He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved﴾, that is, they concealed what reason indicates of the truth of the Qur'an,

﴿concerning the truth﴾, that is, which is not more firm than it in terms of the completeness of its truthfulness, ﴿when it came to them﴾, that is, without allowing themselves time to consider or reflect, so that it might be said that some doubt had occurred to them that led them to what they said. Rather, by hastening to the attack they showed that it is something they do not hesitate about. They also emphasized, in view of their earlier fear for their followers [p. 525], so as to deceive them, and so they said: ﴿Surely﴾, that is, "this is not", ﴿this﴾, that is, the established thing than which nothing is more firmly established, ﴿except sorcery﴾, that is, imagination without any reality, ﴿clear﴾, that is, extremely manifest in its defect, so it proclaims that about itself. So do not be deceived by what is in it that inclines souls and affects hearts. By my life, many people were indeed turned away by this deception, even though [in] their attributing it to sorcery is an acknowledgment of their inability, for a time, until Allah guided some of them, and the matter continued with others until they died in their misguidance. Yet it was fitting for everyone who saw their haste and their burning zeal to know that they were partisan, and that nothing moved them to this but the appetites of the self and the carnal attachments. Ṭufayl ibn ʿAmr al-Dawsī, Dhū al-Nūr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "They ever pressed me about his affair, until I stuffed cotton into my ears out of fear that any of his speech would reach me and tempt me. Then Allah intended good for me, and I said: 'Woe to my mother! By Allah, I am an intelligent, sensible poet, and I have the ability to distinguish the worthless speech from the valuable. So why should I not listen to him? If it is true, I will follow him, and if it is false, I will be informed about it'" – or as he said. He said: "So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'Present to me what you have brought.' When he presented it to me, may my father and mother be his ransom, I had never heard a speech better than it, nor a matter more just than it. So I did not hesitate to accept Islam. Then I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray to Allah that He give me a sign to help me against my people. When I approached the gathering place of my people, there was a light on my forehead, so I feared they would think it was a disfigurement, so I prayed that it be moved, and it moved to the tip of my whip. Allah helped me against my people [so they embraced Islam]."

And when they openly defended this claim without any remnant of knowledge [from] or any report [from] transmitted authority, He explained this, marvelling at their state and making clear their obstinacy, by saying, emphatically, as an indication that what they venture to say of statements that have no basis except blind imitation (taqlid, following without evidence) can only come from a Book or a Messenger: ﴿And We had not given them﴾, meaning that they said this while the fact is that We had not given them, that is, these Arabs, at all, because no Book had ever been sent down to them before the Qur'an. He expressed this with the form of majesty, as an indication that this is a station of great danger and a very rugged place, because it is the root of the religion, so nothing in it is satisfied except by a matter of great weight. He reinforced this meaning by saying: ﴿of books﴾, in the plural form, with the emphasis of negation through the preposition [before your comprehensive Book] ﴿which they study﴾, meaning they renew their study of them at all times. Thus these books are strongly unified in their indication, being in agreement on one meaning and transmitted by numerous chains in their view, with no doubt about their matter, so that this would be a cause for attacking the Qur'an if it contradicted those books. ﴿Nor did We send﴾ [Saba′: 34], meaning a sending free of any doubt, owing to its suitability to the greatness We possess, ﴿to them﴾ [meaning specifically, in the sense that that Messenger is commanded to address them by their very persons, so they are intended directly, and not that they are included in a general address, or intended by way of enjoining good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf, commanding what is right) throughout the time that] ﴿before you﴾, meaning [before your sending, the comprehensive one, which is a sending for every people, so that Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them, are excluded, for they were in some part of past time; or that what is meant] is the interval (al-fatra, the period of no messenger) after ʿIsa, peace be upon him, as was previously cited in the commentary on Surat al-Sajda from Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil. It is also possible that what is meant is after Isma'il, peace be upon him, because ʿIsa, peace be upon him, although he sent his messengers to the Arabs, was not sent [except] to his own people, and his sending to others was only by way of enjoining good. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had a message only to a group or two of them. [It may be said]: what indicates it is that the absolute inclusion of all past time, by the bare form without a governing preposition, shows that what is meant is only the negation of a sending with this falsehood that they claimed, not the sending in absolute terms. He emphasized the negation by saying: ﴿any warner﴾, meaning so that there would be with them a statement from him that opposes the face of the Qur'an, which would then be a basis for them to attack it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 45:

When he had negated the cause of blame, he mentioned the preventive factor that necessitates submission, saying: (p-528) ﴿And they denied﴾, i.e., they did what they did, the situation being that ﴿those before them﴾ had denied, i.e., the people of Nuh and those after them hastened to what these [people] hastened to, because denial was in their natures on account of the coarseness and arrogance that they had. ﴿And they did not reach﴾, i.e., these [people], ﴿one-tenth of what We had given them﴾, i.e., a small tenth of what We had given those [earlier peoples] of strength in bodies and wealth and capacity [in everything] of intellects, length of lifespans, and freedom from preoccupations. ﴿So they denied﴾ [i.e.,] because of the obstinacy with which they had been imprinted, [and he made the pronoun singular as it rightly is, and explicitly so that the nun previously was for majesty, not for plurality, to repel a quibbler, so he said]: ﴿My messengers﴾.

Since their audacity against the messengers was the cause of their destruction in wondrous ways, it became a lasting example struck until the Day of Resurrection, and the blessings that had been spread out for them did not avail them in warding off the vengeances. It was fitting that it be said to the one who sees it or hears of it: ﴿Then how was My rejection?﴾ [i.e., in what it had of severity, which was like a natural disposition], meaning My rejection of those who denied My messengers, so that the question would be an alert to this addressee and a summons to him to submission, out of fear that what befell them might befall him if he did the like of what they did [whether the rejection was at the lowest of its degrees, as We made it a cause of the suspension of causes, or at its highest, as We sent down upon the people of Nuh, peace be upon him, and those like them (p-529) and poured down torment and annihilation, the destruction being inflicted by the calamity, as indicated by the two readings of deleting and affirming the yā' (of nakīr)].

When he had refuted all their doubts and softened their obstinacy through warning, and they became fit to accept admonition, [and among what they accused him of, may he be far from it, were madness and deliberately lying,] He commanded him to address them with it, lightening it for him so that they would not flee from its length. So He said: ﴿Say﴾. He emphasized it further, to draw them into attending to it, and said: ﴿I only admonish you with one thing﴾, meaning: listen, and do not flee out of fear that I will bore you. Then He resumed his speech as an explanation of it: ﴿that you stand up﴾, meaning: that you direct your souls toward recognizing the truth. He expressed it with "standing" to indicate striving. ﴿for Allah﴾, meaning the One than whom there is nothing greater, in sincerity and with awareness of His greatness through the favors He has bestowed upon you [not for the purpose of contention]. Your condition being ﴿in pairs﴾, meaning two by two, [and He placed it first to indicate that most people are deficient in intellect], ﴿and singly﴾, meaning one by one. Whoever trusts himself in the soundness of his intellect and the originality of his judgment stands alone, so that his secret is purer and more conducive to the clarity of his thought. Whoever fears for himself joins another to himself, so that the other may remind him if he forgets and correct him if he deviates. Since this category is the most common among people, He placed it first and did not mention the others, indicating that when they are in these two conditions it is more fitting for them (p-530) to know the truth without any admixture of partisanship, unlike what occurs in a large gathering of disputation and verbiage that prevents the refining of opinion, the cultivation of thought, and the purification of meanings.

Since what He asked of them for this purpose is great and deserving of such attention, He indicated it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿then reflect﴾, meaning: strive, after deliberation and prolonged consideration, in thinking about what you have ascribed to your companion of madness. Since his ﷺ distance from this is a matter beyond dispute, He resumed His speech [specifying by the expression "companion"], emphasizing it as a refutation of them and an alert to the manifestness of the content of this negation: ﴿Your companion is not mad﴾, meaning: the one who called you to Allah, whom you have tested as a child, a youth, a young man, and a man of middle age. He intensified the negation by saying ﴿any madness﴾, and specified it because it is something that could befall a person. He did not turn to lying, because it is not possible for one who has lived among people for a long life and a lasting age, accompanying them by night and day, morning and evening, secretly and openly, in ease and hardship, and who is the highest of them in aspiration, the most complete of them in manliness, the purest of them in disposition, the most apparent of them in character, and the farthest of them from the courtyard of vileness, to lie absolutely. How much more so regarding what opposes their desires, and how much more so regarding what is ascribed to Allah. How much more so when His speech, in which lying is attributed to him, is inimitable by virtue of its wisdoms and rulings, its eloquence and meanings, which have baffled understandings.

Since this has established, as information and understanding, his innocence of all that they slandered him with, He confined his matter to the admonition against destruction. He said, alerting that what he brought them is not claimed except by one of two men: either a madman, or a truthful man who is the most perfect of men. The first has been negated, so the second is established: ﴿He is only a warner to you﴾, meaning: [that is, the one spoken of himself], whose warning is specifically for you and whose intention is your deliverance. [He magnified the matter of punishment by depicting it as one who has an instrument of seizure encompassing the one he intends], so He said: ﴿before a severe punishment﴾ [meaning] before the descent of ﴿a severe punishment﴾, overpowering, from which there is no escape; if you do not return to Him, it will befall you swiftly. Al-Bukhari related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ ascended al-Safa one day and said: 'O morning!' So Quraysh gathered around him and said: 'What is the matter with you?' He said: 'Tell me, if I informed you that an enemy would attack you in the morning or in the evening, would you not believe me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' Abu Lahab said: 'Ruin to you! Did you gather us for this?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1]."

Since this has been removed from him by what has been said, there remained the possibility that he sought some worldly end, so he negated that too by his command in His saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to the disbelievers: ﴿"Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours"﴾, that is, whatever it may be, ﴿"for my calling you [to faith]"﴾, that is, for my calling you to Him, ﴿"it is yours." I do not want anything from it.﴾ This is a metonymy (kinayah) for: I do not ask you any reward whatsoever, in any way, for my calling you to God. Thus, when it is established that the calling is not for a worldly end, and that the caller is the most intelligent of people, it is established that what moved him to expose himself to those great dangers is only the command of God, to whom belongs all command. Since they sometimes suspected him of seeking a worldly matter, He emphasized his statement: ﴿"My reward is only from God"﴾, that is, from the One above whom there is nothing greater, so one of high aspiration should not seek anything except from Him. ﴿And He is over all things a Witness﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge of His servants' circumstances is complete, so He is worthy to destroy the wrongdoer and exalt the status of the obedient.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 48:

When nothing remained that could cast doubt on the matter of the one who conveys the message, he followed it with the confirmation of the transmission, as a reply to one who seems to say: "Your innocence is established, so who vouches for us regarding the truth of the contents of what you report?" So He said, emphasizing against their denial that what he brings is true [repeating the command "say" to indicate that every statement uttered is a sufficient proof, independent in indicating what preceded it]: ﴿Say﴾ to the one who denied the Tawhid (Oneness of God), the Prophethood and the Resurrection [expressing it with what implies the care that necessitates his victory over every obstinate opponent],

﴿Indeed, my Lord﴾, that is, the One who bestows upon me kinds of favour, who whitens my face at the time of trial, ﴿casts the truth﴾, that is, hurls it in establishing all of that and other things which He wills, hurling it forcefully, (p-533) because He is free of any deliberation, reflection, or contemplation in correcting the meaning or amending its implications, since He is the Knower of the unseen, so He disgraces whoever seeks to extinguish His light with a severe disgrace, and He crushes their falsehood, just as they did in what you ascribed to me [and] in the Tawhid and other matters [not] as you did, in your hastening to support polytheism and to what you described me with, and what you described the thing I brought with. Consequently, grave matters clung to you because of that, among them plain falsehood, and you were not able to produce for my affair, nor for any of that, anything at all that a person of sound intellect would accept.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 49:

When He described him with the utmost of knowledge, He followed it with some of its effects, saying: ﴿Say: The truth has come﴾, that is, the matter that is established, which nothing can remove. He emphasized this as a refutation of them in their supposition that they would prevail, so He said: ﴿And falsehood neither begins nor repeats﴾, that is, while the state is that it does not ﴿begin (yubdi'u) falsehood﴾ [that is, that in which you are, and other than it, in every state wherein its branching out has occurred over the passing of days, ﴿nor does it repeat (yu'idu)﴾]. Rather it is like an inanimate thing with no movement at all, because whatever its owner speaks of in his matter after this clarification, he is exposed. So if you do not turn back from it willingly, you will return while you are humiliated and unwilling. The summary is that this is a metaphor for its destruction by that which shakes the soul and dismisses thought, by representing it as one whose movement has been cut off and whose strength has gone, to the point that there is no hope for it in any way.

And when nothing remained after this except that they would say, out of obstinacy, "You are astray," (when he is neither mad nor a liar, but something has befallen you that has led you astray from the clear path), he said: **"Say"**, meaning to these obstinate people, by way of appeal, with what is in your words of fairness and teaching of good manners: **"If I go astray"**, meaning from the way, on the basis of supposition, **"then I only go astray to my own detriment."** Since God Most High has made the intellect ('aql) an intellect that prevents error and forbids desire, and since error comes only from the distractions of the self with its appetites and private interests, the implied meaning is: "by the distractions in my self that are opposed to the intellect." He alluded to this by saying: **"to my own detriment"**, because when error overcomes something, its matter becomes manifest, its defect becomes clear, and its shame becomes unavoidable, and its bearer comes to a state where he knows nothing that benefits and cannot return. For this reason he turns to foolishness and mutual abuse, as has happened in all your schools of thought, because God Most High made sound intellects the criterion for this. Whenever the ways of [the truth] are mentioned and clarified, the matter of falsehood becomes apparent and is exposed. [Since the self is inclined, indeed reaching out, toward falsehood, he expressed error with the bare form (ḍalla) and guidance with the reflexive form (ihtadā), indicating that there must be in it (p-535) a guide and a remedy. He expressed it with the particle of doubt (in) as a use of fairness, and so he said]: **"And if I am guided, it is only by what my Lord reveals to me"**, meaning my guidance is only by what **"my Lord reveals to me"**, that is, the One who is good to me, not by anything else. Therefore error is not possible in it, because the self has no share in it at all, and no one can find any point of criticism against any part of it. My guidance is for my own self. So the verse outwardly is a descent to their level, and inwardly it is a guidance to them to straighten their looking, correct it, refine their thinking and sharpen it. It is of the device of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are mentioned and each omits what the other supplies): it first omitted that error is from himself, by what is indicated in the second clause, which is that guidance is from the revelation; and second, it omitted that guidance is for him, by what is indicated in the first clause, which is that error is upon him. Then he gave the reason for both error and guidance with his saying: **"Indeed He is All-Hearing, Near"**, meaning: my Lord hears nothing that is hidden from Him of the state of whoever lies about Him, so He is worthy to expose him, just as He exposed you in all that you claim. Nothing is far from Him, so that He would need delay to perceive it for the sake of covering a distance or the like; rather He perceives everything He wills whenever He wills.

The verse is a guidance from God Most High that, although He created for the human being an intellect that does not go astray or deviate, He surrounded it with cutting obstacles of appetites, private interests, laziness and lethargy, so that hardly anyone is safe from them except whom God protects. Since this is so, He, glorified be He, sent down books which are pure intellect, and sent messengers whom He stripped of those obstacles, so that their characters became their laws (*sharā'i'*). Therefore every person must follow His messengers who have passed on with His books, considering his own intellect suspect and rejecting his own opinion, as the Companions (may God be pleased with them) did, so that he may be a believer in the unseen with true belief, and enters into His saying Most High in Surat Fatir: **"You only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen"** [Fatir: 18], and is not one who reaches for it from a distant place after the veil has been removed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 51:

When he had refuted their doubts and concluded the attributes of Him with what entails seizing those who oppose Him, he said, linking it to ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers﴾ [Saba': 31], ﴿And if you could see﴾, meaning, there would be a sight from you, ﴿when they are terrified﴾, meaning, they will be terrified by Our seizing them in this world and the Hereafter. However, he expressed it in the past tense, and likewise in the verbs that come after this, because what Allah will do in the future is as what has already occurred and been realized, owing to its certainty. ﴿Then there is no escape﴾, meaning, as a consequence of that terror, there is no escape for them from Us, because they are in Our grip, ﴿and you would see a dreadful matter and a terrible affair﴾. He belittled their situation by using the passive voice, so he said: ﴿And they will be seized﴾, meaning, at the time of terror, by everyone whom We command to seize them, whether before death or after it. And since nearness makes it easy to seize what one wants to seize, he said: ﴿from a near place﴾, meaning, a seizure for which nothing is easier, for the One who seizes, glory be to Him, is able, and there is no distance between Him and anything; rather, He is closer to it than its own self.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 34, verse 52:**

﴿And they will say﴾, that is, at the time of seizure and of witnessing the reward and the punishment: ﴿"We believe in it"﴾, that is, in the One whose belief was required of us, "and we have rejected it." The closer reading is that the "it" refers to [the Qur'an], which they had called a fabricated lie. ﴿And how⁠﴾, that is, how and from where, ﴿can they reach it?⁠﴾ That is, how can they obtain (al-tanawush) faith or some of its fruits? It seems he used this expression because it is also applied to returning. So the meaning is that this was far beyond them, since it is possible only by their returning to the world, which is the abode of action. And how could they have that? This is an illustration of their situation, in their seeking that their faith benefit them at that time, as the faith of the believers benefited them in the world, by comparison with a person who wants to take something from a height the way another takes it easily from the distance of an arm's length, without any effort. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr (on the authority of 'Asim) lengthened it because they read it with a hamza (hamz). It has been said that the hamza is placed on a damma-marked waw, as it was hamzed in some forms and as it was made to stop, so that its wording matches its meaning. The correct view is that it is not of this kind, because the condition for hamzing a waw marked with a constant damma is that it not be assimilated into it when it is in the middle of the word, as in al-ta'awwud, and that the verb does not allow forms like tanawala and ta'awana. It has been reported from Abu 'Amr that its meaning with the hamza is reaching from a distance, from their saying na'asha (with a hamza) when someone became slow and fell behind; al-nay'sh is a movement in slowness, and al-na'sh also means taking. In that case the hamza is original. The rest read it with a waw, like al-tanawul in wording and meaning. So the reading with the pure waw indicates that they want an easy reaching while the object is far away in place, (p-٥٣٨) and the reading with the hamza indicates that their wanting was delayed and slowed until its time had passed. Thus it combines distance of place with distance of time.

Since a distant thing cannot be reached by a person when it is far away, He said: ﴿from a far place⁠﴾. For after the veil is lifted at the coming of the punishment, faith does not benefit.

﴿And [they had] already﴾ [i.e.] how could they have that [faith] when the situation is that they had ﴿disbelieved in it﴾, i.e., in that which they were asked to believe in, hoping for it and as its reward, ﴿before﴾, i.e., in the abode of action, while the situation is that, at the time of their disbelief, they cast about concerning the matter to which they were called, with what they hurl of speech, a very swift hurling without deliberation or reflection, ﴿in the unseen﴾ [i.e.] from the stonings of conjectures, which is the doubt (*shubhah*) whose refutation has preceded in this surah and elsewhere, namely their deeming resurrection and other things improbable, which God has informed of.

Since a thing cannot strike what it hurls while it is absent from it, especially with distance, [God] said, informing that they are far removed from knowledge of what they say, along with His being very far from the state of those about whom they speak, whether it be the Qur'an, the Prophet (ﷺ), or the Gathering (*hashr*), Paradise and Hell: ﴿from a far place﴾. This is contrary to the casting of the All-Knowing of the unseen, for He is from a near place, so He is known and firmly attached to the truth.

When he indicated the distance of faith from them at the time they wished to grasp it, after its opportunity had passed, and its exaltedness above them when they disparaged it in the abode of action, he expressed their two states in (p. 539) a manner that encompasses the fruits of faith, from entering the Gardens to the good pleasure of the Most Merciful, by His saying: ﴿And a barrier will be placed﴾, using the passive form to indicate that the barrier comes about in the easiest manner, and because what is painful to them is the barrier itself, not that it comes from a specific person: ﴿between them and what they desire﴾, meaning they incline toward it with a great inclination, owing to the effect of their disparagement and the acceptance of their faith at the sight of [the] punishment, and owing to their obtaining some of its fruits, such as the goodness of reward [as a person among them sees, while he is in the throes of the Fire, his seat in Paradise, which would have been his had he believed, and he cannot reach it by any means; and if the reaching of it is imagined for him, and he aims for it but is prevented from it, that is more painful]. ﴿As was done﴾ [meaning] in the easiest manner ﴿with their likes﴾, meaning those who disbelieved like them, ﴿before﴾, meaning before [their time]. Their condition [was] like their condition in disbelief and faith, and in felicity and loss. Our command did not fail with any nation among the nations; rather, whenever a nation denied its messenger, We seized it. If We made them taste Our might, they submitted and humbled themselves, but We did not accept that from them, nor did it benefit them at all, neither by withholding Our destruction of them nor by their attaining any good after their destruction. ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf 37]. Then he gave the reason for the non-attainment of the aim in each of the two states by His saying, emphasizing their denial that they have any doubt about any part of their affair: ﴿Indeed they were﴾, meaning (p. 540) in the abode of acceptance, a state that was like an innate disposition for them, ﴿in doubt﴾, meaning about everything Our messengers tell them from Us regarding recompense or otherwise, ﴿disquieting﴾, meaning causing [in] disquiet. It is eloquent in its kind, as one says, "a wonder that is wondrous," or it is one who falls into doubt, as one says, "poetry of a poet," meaning, one possessed of poetry. How then could their disparagement be accepted, or take effect, or any good fruit come to them, when they are without insight into any part of their affair? Rather, they were doubting Our power and Our greatness. So it is fitting for wisdom that We make the greatness manifest to them through punishment [for them] and reward for Our beloved ones who opposed them for Our sake, so that it becomes clear that they believe [in it] when the praise appears in its fullest manifestation, either in the Hereafter or in its preliminaries. Thus the secret of the explicit statement became evident in His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾ [Saba 1], and that He, glory be to Him, placed a barrier between them and what they wish. It thus became clear that He is the owner of everything, so it is correct that to Him belongs praise in the first life and in every state, and its last part has embraced its first, and its ending has joined with what connects to it. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One sought for help, and to Him is the return and the final resort.
